God is known in her citadels when He supports her.
For behold, the kings gathered; they came together.
They saw and thus marveled; they were troubled and shaken.
Trembling seized them; there were pangs like a woman giving birth.
With a violent wind Thou wilt shatter the ships of Tarshish.
Just as we heard, so we saw in the city of the Lord of powers, in our God’s city; God founded her for ever. Diapsalma.
While the sacrifice was being consumed, the priests offered prayer—the priests and everyone—with Jonathan beginning and the others responding, as Nehemiah did.
Esdras blessed the Lord, the great God. All the people answered and said, “Amen,” lifting their hands, and they bowed and worshiped the Lord with their faces to the ground.
The priests sang the hymns in response.

They laid the foundation for building the Lord’s house, and the priests stood in their vestments with trumpets, and the Levites, sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise the Lord according to the directions of David king of Israel.

They answered in praise and thanksgiving to the Lord: “For it is good, for His mercy toward Israel endures for ever.” All the people sounded a great cry of praise to the Lord at the founding of the Lord’s house.

These same things were related in the records and in the memoirs concerning Nehemiah, and also how, in establishing a library, he gathered together the books concerning the kings and prophets, the writings of David, and kings’ letters concerning dedicated gifts.
Then Darius the king issued a decision and made a search in the libraries where the treasury is kept in Babylon.
A scroll was found in a city, in the citadel of the city of the Medes, and this was written in it: “Memorandum:

In the first year of Cyrus the king, King Cyrus issued a decision concerning the house of God in Jerusalem: Let the house be built, and the place where they sacrifice the sacrifices. He set an elevation: sixty cubits high and sixty cubits wide,
with three courses of strong stone and one wooden course. The expense will be paid from the king’s house.

And let the silver and gold vessels of God’s house, which Nabouchodonosor took from the house in Jerusalem and carried to Babylon, be given back and go to the sanctuary in Jerusalem, to the place where they were set in God’s house.”
For us who have undertaken the hard work of abridgement, the task is not easy; it involves sweat and sleeplessness.
My son, beware of making many books; there is no limit, and much study is weariness of the flesh.

For just as the architect of a new house must consider its whole foundation, while the person undertaking its encaustic work and painting must examine what is suitable for decoration, so, I think, it is with us.
According to the grace of God given to me, I laid a foundation as a wise master builder, and another builds upon it. But let each one watch how he builds upon it.
For no one can lay another foundation besides the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.
Whoever saw the high priest’s appearance was wounded in mind, for his face and altered complexion revealed his soul’s anguish.
The king said to me, “Why is your face distressed when you are not unwell? This is nothing but distress of heart.” I became very greatly afraid.
I said to the king, “May the king live for ever! Why should my face not be distressed, since the city, the home of my fathers’ tombs, has been laid waste and its gates have been consumed by fire?”
People also rushed out of their houses in crowds for a public supplication, because the place was about to be treated with contempt.
Blow a trumpet in Zion! Consecrate a fast; proclaim a service.
Gather the people; consecrate the congregation. Choose elders; gather infants nursing at breasts. Let the bridegroom leave his bedroom and the bride her bridal chamber.

In the midst of the altar’s platform the priests who minister to the Lord will weep and say, “Spare Thy people, Lord, and do not give Thine inheritance to reproach, for nations to rule over them, so that they do not say among the nations, ‘Where is their God?’”

triples.relationship: Thematic comparison of divine protection of the holy city
triples.rationale: The letter credits God with driving out opponents arrayed against the holy city. The psalm describes God supporting His city while assembled kings are troubled and shaken. Both locate the city's security in God's action against threatening rulers; the psalm is not identified as a prediction or account of this particular expulsion.

triples.relationship: Liturgical parallel of a leader and answering assembly
triples.rationale: Jonathan begins the prayer while the priests and others respond during the sacrifice; Esdras blesses the Lord and all the people answer Amen. Both depict public prayer with a leader and a responding congregation. The occasions remain distinct; Maccabees does not specify an Amen response, and Jonathan is not identified with Esdras.

triples.rationale: The priests sing hymns in response after the sacrificial prayer; at the foundation of the Lord's house, priests and Levites participate in answering praise and thanksgiving. The shared practice is responsive temple praise, without identifying the unnamed hymns in Maccabees as Ezra's quoted refrain or equating the ceremonies.

triples.relationship: Archival preservation of royal provisions for sacred gifts
triples.rationale: Nehemiah's reported library includes kings' letters about dedicated gifts. Ezra describes a treasury-library search and a preserved memorandum of Cyrus's provisions for rebuilding the Jerusalem house and returning its gold and silver vessels. Both associate collected written royal records with sacred endowments; Ezra's memorandum is not asserted to be one of Nehemiah's particular letters or in the same archive.

triples.relationship: Literary reflection on the bodily cost of study and writing
triples.rationale: The abridger describes the work of producing the condensed history as sweat and sleeplessness. Ecclesiastes links the making of many books and much study with weariness of the flesh. Both explicitly connect literary work with bodily strain, while the abridger willingly undertakes the task and Ecclesiastes issues a caution.

triples.relationship: Comparison of building metaphors for different responsibilities
triples.rationale: The abridger distinguishes an architect's concern for the whole foundation from the decorator's work to explain historian and abridger roles. Paul distinguishes laying a foundation as a master builder from another person's building upon it. Both use construction roles to distinguish responsibilities; Paul's foundation is explicitly Jesus Christ, and the literary historian is not equated with that foundation.

triples.relationship: Visible facial distress revealing inner sorrow
triples.rationale: Onias's changed face reveals the anguish of his soul to observers. The king reads the speaker's distressed face as distress of heart, and the speaker explains his grief over the devastated city. Both make facial appearance an outward sign of inward sorrow; the threatened temple deposits and the burned city gates are different causes.

triples.rationale: People leave their houses for public supplication because the sanctuary is threatened with contempt, while the priests plead in the surrounding scene. Joel calls the congregation together and has the priests ask that God's inheritance not be given to reproach or foreign rule. Both present communal assembly and priestly petition against disgrace, without treating Heliodorus's mission as the fulfilment of Joel's summons.
